blocks.html: As with all things in nature yet to come into being, we mortals are wont to believe that there was naught before it.
Only darkness. A boundless void. An abyss without end.
Perhaps that was so.
Yet none among us can say with certainty, for we know not where the beginning truly lay, nor when it first came to pass.
And so, as we weave this ancient myth, there is said to have been a being older than all that we now know. Like an ancient Guardian.
When first she became aware of her own existence, she found herself a witness to the passing of something unseen.
Time.
And with Time came a beginning, a starting point from which all things thereafter would unfold.
And from it, the world as we know it would one day come to be.
Yet in those first ages, all things were intangible.
Countless millennia passed beneath the watchful gaze of the Guardian. Quietly, she lingered within the endless swirl of darkness, amidst drifting cosmic dust.
There was not much to see.
At least, not yet.
Perhaps she had intangible thoughts, an intangible soul.
And wondered what all that dust was for.
For even the universe seemed to be learning what it was meant to become.
Then came the stars.
One by one, great lights appeared in the darkness. Brilliant flares danced across the heavens, and wandering stones of rock began to drift through the great expanse.
And, for the first time, there was something to wonder about.
Slowly, the emptiness began to take shape.
And as the universe took its first uncertain steps toward creation, so too did the Guardian.
Heavenly bodies gathered throughout the heavens, and the universe found its equilibrium.
All that was once intangible became tangible.
And so did the Guardian, whose soul became a bright, beautiful star.
Down from the heavens it came, falling upon our world.
And there, the Guardian continued her watch of Time, no longer upon a cosmic scale.
She watched the world slowly become the world we know today.
But it would be a very long time.
Perhaps the Guardian grew lonely.
So, at some point, as though Time itself had decided to gift something back to her…
Seven stars fell from the night sky.
